product.summary: A phone app that tracks kitchen food from scanned grocery receipts and suggests meals that use it before it spoils.

source.quote: A phone app that keeps track of what is in your kitchen and suggests meals that use up food before it spoils.

evidence.value: Still an idea; nothing built yet

source.quote: Pantry Pal is still an idea. Nothing is built yet.

evidence.value: Landing page and a waitlist of 340 email sign-ups

source.quote: We have a landing page and a waitlist with 340 email sign-ups
Our hope is 2,000 people in the beta

source.quote: 10,000 users by the end of next year, but these are guesses
Users sign in with email.
We store the food they buy and the meals they cook.

source.why: Purchase and meal history is personal data whose leak can embarrass people; allergy data, if stored later, would be health data and make it high.

constraints.text: Total spend in the first year stays within the founders' $12,000 savings

source.quote: $12,000 in total for the first year, everything included

constraints.text: Delete receipt photos once their items are read, as promised on the landing page

source.quote: Receipt photos should be deleted once the items are read; we promised this on the landing page.

goals.note: Get a beta out fast to learn whether people use it

source.quote: Above all, we need to learn quickly whether people use it, so getting a beta out fast is the first thing.
Keeping costs low comes right after that.

goals.note: Simple to operate; no nights fixing servers

source.quote: We do not want to spend nights fixing servers, so anything we run should be simple to operate.

goals.note: Easy to change often after the beta

source.quote: We will need to change things often after the beta, so the design should be easy to change.

unknowns.question: Will Pantry Pal store users' food allergies?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Allergy data is health data: it raises sensitivity to high and brings stricter rules on consent, storage and security.

unknowns.question: Which country will the beta launch in first?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Germany brings GDPR and Canada PIPEDA; the answer decides the hosting region and the privacy duties.

unknowns.question: How many receipts does a typical user scan per week?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Reading receipts is the main processing load and cost; it sizes the receipt-reading service.

unknowns.question: What availability and data-loss tolerance does the beta need?
unknowns.why_it_matters: With no one on call at night, the answer decides how much redundancy and managed hosting to pay for.

assumptions.text: The beta is one region and one small database.
assumptions.why: Two part-time founders, a few thousand projected users and no stated peaks.
